desc: Derive the equivalence: game ends on the N-th distinct first-pick; moves on already-claimed indices are pure turn-consuming filler (passes), so state reduces to (unclaimed count k, pass budget p, parities of remaining piles).
Formalize the reduction: proved by induction that the win/lose outcome depends only on (k, count of odd remaining piles, p mod 2); derived closed-form rule.
Prove the winning condition: Fennec wins iff N=1; or N=3 with ≥1 odd A_i; or N≥4 with odd count of odd A_i; N=2 always Snuke. Verified against all three samples.
Handle edge cases: N=1 (Fennec always), all A_i=1 (winner = parity of N, consistent with rule), large A_i (only parity matters).
Cross-check the rule by brute-force game simulation (DP over small states) for tiny N and A_i ≤ 3 — 0 mismatches across all 120 enumerated instances.
Implement solve() reading N and the list, applying the O(N) parity rule, printing "Fennec"/"Snuke".
